newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi says sees higher 97/98 group oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi says sees higher 97/98 group oper profit.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd said on Thursday that it expects to post a group operating profit of 335 billion yen in the the current business year to March 31, 1998, up 13 percent year-on-year.

Executive managing director Yoshiki Yagi told a news conference that sluggish chip prices nearly halved the firm's operating profit in the information and electronics sectors during the last business year.
He said the firm expects a slight group operating loss to remain in the semiconductor sector this year.
Yagi said Hitachi posted a group appraisal loss on semiconductor-making equipment of 45.5 billion yen in 1996/97 as a result of the sluggish market for chips.
He said Hitachi's operating profit in the electric power plant and industrial machines sector would decrease by more than 10 percent in the current business year.
Yagi said Hitachi plans group capital spending on semiconductors of 150 billion yen in 1997/98, unchanged from last year.

He added that a decline in prices for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) would continue over the next two years. He said 64 MB DRAMs and other new chip products would not start contributing to profits until the second half of the current business year.
